nodes.label: Project Constitution (.specify/memory/constitution.md)
nodes.rationale: Constitution is treated as non-negotiable authority: any MUST-principle violation is automatically CRITICAL in /speckit-analyze and /speckit-converge and must be fixed by adjusting spec/plan/tasks, never by diluting or reinterpreting the principle.

nodes.label: "Unit Tests for English" checklist philosophy
nodes.author: github-spec-kit
nodes.rationale: Checklists validate the quality of requirements writing (completeness, clarity, consistency, measurability, coverage), not implementation behavior; treats English requirements as code needing unit tests, explicitly prohibiting items like 'Verify X works' in favor of 'Is X clearly specified?'.

nodes.label: Append-only, never-rewrite operating constraint
nodes.author: github-spec-kit
nodes.rationale: speckit-converge's only permitted write is appending a new Phase N: Convergence section to tasks.md; it must never modify spec.md/plan.md/application code or renumber existing tasks, and must leave tasks.md byte-for-byte unchanged when nothing remains, so the command is safely idempotent/re-runnable and traceable.

nodes.label: Human review-gate pattern (review-spec / review-plan)
nodes.author: GitHub
nodes.rationale: Gate steps between specify->plan and plan->tasks require explicit approve/reject so a human can abort the pipeline before downstream planning/task work is wasted on a flawed spec or plan; the integration list is an advisory, non-exhaustive hint (any: [...]) rather than a closed set, so the workflow runs against any integration providing the four core commands.
